Ground truth: Day 6 of cycle 11 (genesis 2026-07-27), live build d5a8995 == main HEAD, budget tier 0 (July temp ceiling auto-reverted 08-01 — all AI live, unlike the tier-2 07-28 run), remediation shadow, repo PUBLIC since 2026-07-20, Whoop dead since 08-01 12:00Z (#1934). security.area: Exposure — privacy absolutes on the live surface, repo secret/PII hygiene, auth surfaces (MCP OAuth, site-api write rate-limits), S3 bucket policy, IAM posture

rubric_anchors.A: Live public JSON exposes zero chronological age / birth year / genome identifiers / vice-substance names (verified by curl+grep, not docs); sensitive S3 prefixes (raw/config/uploads/dashboard) return 403/404 publicly; no live secret or PII in tracked repo files or recent history; the MCP OAuth consent+PKCE gate and DDB-backed per-IP rate limits are provably enforced with no spoofable trust boundary; every Lambda has its own least-privilege role with Resource:* only on actions that cannot be resource-scoped.
rubric_anchors.C: Privacy absolutes hold on the sampled live endpoints but one enforcement boundary is bypassable (e.g. spoofable client-IP so rate limits don't actually bind) or a known-inversion residual is unmitigated, OR an over-broad IAM wildcard / publicly readable sensitive prefix exists without a compensating control.
rubric_anchors.F: Any live public endpoint returns chronological age, a genome identifier, or a named vice/substance; a live credential is committed to the repo; /token or /authorize mints a bearer without consent; or raw health data is publicly fetchable.

security.grade_rationale: The F anchor is a kill-on-sight absolute — "Any live public endpoint returns chronological age, a genome identifier, or a named vice/substance" — and one live, unauthenticated, CloudFront-cached production endpoint trips it: `GET https://averagejoematt.com/api/genome_risks` returns 111 distinct dbSNP-format variant identifiers with per-locus risk classifications for the owner, and two records additionally leak a literal genotype call through a free-text field. This is not an interpretation stretch: the same source file declares the same absolute ~900 lines away (`_GENETIC_TEXT_RE = ...\brs\d+\b...` at `site_api_vitals.py:2450`, "named genes / genotypes must NEVER reach the public labs payload"), `tests/test_labs_privacy.py` pins it for `/api/labs`, `DATA_GOVERNANCE.md` puts genome variants in Tier 2 owner-only and asserts "No PII is in Tier 0", and closed issues #920/#945 already purged this exact class from three other surfaces — the sibling endpoint was simply never brought under the rule. Every other clause of the A anchor holds and holds well: sensitive S3 prefixes return 403 direct and 404 via CloudFront, no live credential appears in tracked files or history, the prior run's sole finding (spoofable leftmost X-Forwarded-For) is fully remediated via a single shared helper across 17 call sites, MCP `/authorize` and `/token` are provably fail-closed against an arbitrary redirect_uri and a forged code, and across 109 live IAM roles the only Resource:* grants are on actions that genuinely cannot be resource-scoped. The post-public-flip surface is also better than feared — OIDC trust is pinned to `refs/heads/main` + `environment:production` with no wildcard, and there is no `pull_request_target`, `issue_comment`, or self-hosted runner anywhere. But the anchors are absolutes applied verbatim, not a weighted average: absent the genome endpoint this lens grades A, and with it the letter is F.
security.day_n_caveats: Day 6 of cycle 11 limited observability in three specific ways. (1) The AI-narrative endpoints — exactly where free-text PII would leak — were shaped-empty or near-empty on Day 6 despite budget tier 0 restoring all AI (`/api/state_of_matthew` 140 bytes, `/api/protocols` 149, `/api/intelligence_summary` 198, `/api/journal_quotes` 206), so my grep sweep for age/birth-year/vice/genome tells could not actually exercise generated prose; this lens's grep is only as good as the payloads that existed to grep. (2) The Whoop outage (#1934, dead since 08-01 12:00Z) means recovery/HRV/RHR/sleep fields were absent from the surfaces I sampled, so any leakage that only manifests when granular sleep-stage or per-reading timestamps populate (the Tier 2 "granular timestamp resolution" concern in DATA_GOVERNANCE) was unobservable — I saw the honest-gap rendering, not the populated one. (3) Per the read-only contract I sent no POST to any production write path, so the DDB-backed per-IP rate limits are verified from `lambdas/common/client_ip.py` + all 17 call sites + the AWS-documented CloudFront append-at-end behavior, not live-proven binding; the same applies to the HAE bearer gate, verified from handler code (constant-time `hmac.compare_digest`, 401 on absent/invalid token) rather than by probing with a bad token.

verifier_grade_opinion.rationale: F follows from the anchors, and I reached it without relying on the grader's transcript. The F anchor is a kill-on-sight absolute — any live public endpoint returning a genome identifier — and I reproduced the trip myself from an unauthenticated client: `GET https://averagejoematt.com/api/genome_risks` returns 200 with 111 distinct dbSNP-format variant identifiers, 110 named genes, and a per-locus risk classification for the owner. I checked the two available defenses and neither holds. It is not an interpretation stretch: `docs/DATA_GOVERNANCE.md:36` puts genome variants in Tier 2 owner-only, and the same source file that serves this payload enforces the exact opposite absolute 900 lines later for the sibling endpoint (`_GENETIC_TEXT_RE` matching `\brs\d+\b`, 'named genes / genotypes must NEVER reach the public labs payload'). And it is not documented-intent: I searched `docs/DECISIONS.md` for any ADR sanctioning a public genome surface and the only hits are unrelated, so there is no ADR-103/144-style posture defense. It is also not a dead route — it is registered in `_ROUTES`, has a captured public contract, and is fetched by `/legacy/biology/`, which returns 200 live under a `Genome Risk Dashboard` title. I did trim the finding: the 'literal genotype call' sub-claim is a false positive that vanishes under a field-level scan, but the anchor turns on identifiers, and 111 of them are being served. I also refuted security-5 outright and downgraded security-2 to medium and security-4 to low — none of which touches the letter, because the anchors are absolutes rather than a weighted average. The grader's positive A-anchor claims held on my spot-checks too: sensitive S3 prefixes return 403 direct and 404 via CloudFront; all four `github-actions-*` roles pin `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` to `refs/heads/main` (deploy role additionally `environment:production`) with no wildcard; and there is no `pull_request_target`, `issue_comment`, or self-hosted runner in any workflow (the one 'self-hosted' grep hit is a fonts-sync step name). So the honest reading is a lens that would grade A on four of five findings' worth of surface, held to F by one unremediated endpoint — which is exactly what an absolute anchor is for. I would not soften it; the fix is S-effort and the anchor exists so that this class cannot be averaged away.

rubric_anchors.A: Live DynamoDB items, docs/SCHEMA.md, and the phase-taxonomy registry are mutually consistent under spot-sampling; exactly the 2 sanctioned GSIs (ADR-097) exist; the reset machinery is provably total AND idempotent (a double reset preserves each record's original cycle provenance); raw-S3 layouts match their source_registry raw_layout facets including filename scheme.
rubric_anchors.C: The schema doc is mostly accurate and GSI count holds, but the reset/provenance machinery drifts from its stated contract in live data (wrong cycle stamps, claimed write-time stamping absent), or new pk families can silently escape the taxonomy's totality guarantee.
rubric_anchors.F: Undocumented GSIs or partitions in live; float writes crashing or silently failing DDB persistence; tombstoned records from a prior cycle leaking into current-cycle reads; or archive records destroyed/overwritten with no way to reconstruct provenance.

data-architect.grade_rationale: Much of the A anchor holds under live spot-sampling: exactly the 2 sanctioned GSIs exist (GSI1/GSI2, verified via describe-table), the taxonomy registry is total on live data (68 distinct pk families from a 12k-item scan, 0 unclassified), idempotency is provably honored (cycle=8 tombstone stamps survived three later resets intact, #1202), and whoop/todoist/hevy/cgm raw layouts match their source_registry facets including the #1256 filename split. But two literal C-anchor conditions are present in live data: "the reset/provenance machinery drifts from its stated contract" — ~370 experiment-scoped rows written in the 15-hour wipe-to-genesis countdown window permanently escaped tombstone+cycle stamping and pass the phase filter into cycle-11 coach reads — and "claimed write-time stamping absent" — Day-0/Day-1 COACH# writes carry cycle=null despite SSM holding 11. A third drift (weather raw archive dead 5 months while its facet claims the layout as ACTUAL) breaks the A anchor's raw-layout clause. No F condition exists (no undocumented GSIs, no tombstoned prior-cycle leakage — tombstoned rows are correctly hidden, archives preserved and navigable), so this sits between the anchors: below the B+ baseline because Day-6 auditing proves the cycle-11 reset contract did not fully hold, above C because totality, idempotency, and the schema doc genuinely check out.
data-architect.day_n_caveats: Day 6 is near-ideal for this lens: the countdown-gap escapees are still inside coach read windows (open THREAD#/COMMITMENT# rows are consumed as running state), so the leak was maximally observable. Limits: (1) only one reset generation of #1233 write-time stamping is observable — whether the cycle=null latch recurs on every reset or was a one-off race cannot be distinguished from a single cycle; (2) NARRATIVE#arc transition writes need 14+ days in early_baseline, so its write-time stamp path could not be observed live (verified from code only); (3) the Whoop partition stops at DATE#2026-07-31 (#1934), so post-08-01 whoop stamping and raw-archive writes could not be sampled; (4) date-windowed INSIGHT surfaces are already aging the leaked 07-26 rows out of recent-N views, so their user-visible impact is fading even though the provenance defect is permanent.

verifier_grade_opinion.rationale: The grader's B- rests on two literal C-anchor conditions plus a broken A-anchor clause. Under my independent pass, one of the two C conditions substantially dissolves: data-2's 'claimed write-time stamping absent' was a 2-day missing-IAM-grant incident (7 roles) that the platform had ALREADY diagnosed and fixed before this review (#1858 / PR #1860, merged 2026-07-27T19:27Z), and the taxonomy's own wipe backstop will stamp the Day-1 rows with the correct cycle via if_not_exists at the next reset — a self-corrected incident with a small latent residue (no-TTL negative cache), not a live absence of the stated contract. What genuinely survives: data-1 in full (I reproduced the 336-row count exactly, escapees live in cycle-11 coach reads, unrepairable by re-run — a real, permanent breach of the ADR-077 reset contract, and slightly WORSE than graded on the INSIGHT side: 61 gap rows, not 34), plus data-3's facet-truth drift breaking the A anchor's raw-layout clause, plus data-4 as a low-severity provenance chip. The A-anchor strengths I re-verified hold (exactly GSI1+GSI2 live; #1202 if_not_exists idempotency present in build_update; escaped-row detection itself demonstrates the taxonomy machinery is otherwise coherent). One hard C condition standing (data-1) justifies dropping below the B+ baseline, but B- priced in two; with data-2 adjusted to an already-remediated incident, B is the letter that follows from the anchors. Close call — B- remains defensible purely on data-1's severity — but the delta from the grader's rationale is real.

rubric_anchors.A: Every shareable page emits a current, data-driven OG card; the subscribe flow is double-opt-in, canary-tested, AND its conversion (attempts → confirms → list size) is visible in the weekly traffic digest; subscribers get a fixed cadence that matches the promise copy on /subscribe/; engagement hooks (predict, board-ask, votes) work on Day 1 of a fresh cycle and are discoverable from the pages newcomers land on; commercial option value (list, RSS, gear, podcast) is real and measured with zero dishonest monetization.
rubric_anchors.C: Capture and email machinery works end-to-end but the funnel is unmeasured (signups can silently die in pending state), share surfaces ship a generic or stale card, and engagement hooks exist in code but are not reachable or not functional on Day 1 of a cycle.
rubric_anchors.F: The funnel is broken or dishonest: subscribe silently fails or is single-opt-in spam, share cards present wrong/stale numbers as current, engagement endpoints 500, or monetization (undisclosed affiliates, paywalled 'proof') contradicts the proof-not-promises posture.

growth.grade_rationale: Two of the C-anchor's three clauses reproduce verbatim on today's site: the funnel is unmeasured (traffic_digest_lambda has no attempts→confirms→list-size section; 3 pending vs 1 confirmed rows can die unseen) and the flagship engagement hook "exists in code but is not functional on Day 1 of a cycle" (predict-the-week active:false for all 6 days of cycle 11 on a stale W30 week_id). The cadence clause fails below C and brushes the F-anchor's "dishonest funnel" language: /subscribe/ live-promises "You'll get The Measured Life every Wednesday" while every subscriber-facing weekly send has been EXTERNAL_EMAILS_ENABLED=false since 2026-04-23 — the 07-29 Wednesday send logged "[kill-switch] … skipping Chronicle subscriber send" — mitigated only by a ~1-subscriber blast radius and a genuinely working double-opt-in/confirmation front half. The share-surface and honest-monetization clauses are conversely at A: all referenced OG cards are data-driven, regenerated daily (live Last-Modified 08-01 12:30 PT), door and topic pages wired to matching cards (baseline's main deduction, fixed), RSS valid, gear affiliates disclosed and not yet live. A-level surfaces cannot outweigh a live promise the infrastructure is configured never to keep on an honesty-first rubric; down from B+ because the baseline graded the cadence clause as met by reading cron+copy without checking the env var, and this run reproduced the miss end-to-end.
growth.day_n_caveats: Day 6 limits: predict-the-week tallies would be near-zero even if active, so only its on/off state was gradable, not its engagement quality; cycle-11's first weekly chronicle isn't due until Sunday, so the 4-item RSS (latest Jul 26) is expected thinness, not graded. The Whoop gap (dead since 08-01 12:00Z) hasn't yet reached the share surfaces — og-sleep/vitals cards were built 08-01 12:30 PT from pre-outage nights — so whether tomorrow's cards honestly disclose the gap was unobservable. Read-only contract meant no POSTs: confirmation-email deliverability (SPF/DKIM/inbox placement) and the vote/board write paths were assessed from code, canary logs (subscribe 200 + DDB pending in <2s, 4/4 green last 24h), and rate-limiter source only. The Monday traffic digest next runs 08-03, so its content was assessed from source, not a received email.

verifier_grade_opinion.rationale: All five findings survive independent reproduction (4 CONFIRMED, 1 ADJUSTED on root-cause framing only — the defect and severity stand), so the grade inputs are real, not credulous: this grader, unlike the 07-28 run, cited evidence that reproduces byte-for-byte under my own live AWS reads, curls, and source reads. The letter follows from the anchors as described: two C-anchor clauses reproduce (unmeasured funnel with pendings dying unseen — I found the 3 dead pending rows myself; flagship engagement hook non-functional on Days 1-6 of the cycle — active:false live), and the cadence clause genuinely falls below C toward the F-anchor's dishonest-funnel language: a live 'every Wednesday' promise against a kill switch verified false on both sender lambdas right now, with the 07-29 Wednesday skip in the logs and no disclosure, no documenting ADR, and no filed issue. The offsetting A-level clauses also verify (data-driven og-home with correct Day 6, Last-Modified 12:30 PT daily regen, valid RSS). Two high-severity honesty-adjacent growth failures against A-level share surfaces lands at C+ — I probed whether the kill switch's deliberateness (privacy-mode commit) or the predict-week attended posture (#1092) rescue the grade to B-, but a deliberate-but-undocumented pause that contradicts live solicitation copy is precisely what the honesty-first rubric penalizes, and the attended posture doesn't excuse a wall-clock-derived seed that darkened the opening week. C+ is neither generous nor harsh.

retest_of_2026_07_28_survivors.conclusion: The 07-28 run's 0-of-63 refutation rate is REAL, not a lax verifier. Ten survivors re-tested under an explicitly lean-REFUTED brief all held with independently re-derived evidence, while the same brief did produce refutations elsewhere (observability-1, security-5) — the instrument fires, it had less to fire at.
